repaired.name: Scenario

diagnosis.summary: The candidate uses a 1000 ms wrapper period with a threshold of 30, causing the action to fire at 29000 ms. The IR requires a 30-second duration, which is 30000 ms. With a 1000 ms period, the first tick counts at t=0, so the action should fire at the 30th tick (t=29000) only if the threshold is 30. However, the evidence shows the IR waits until 30000 ms (30 seconds), implying the counter must reach 301 ticks (0 to 300) or the threshold calculation in the candidate is misaligned with the expected 30-second duration relative to the 1000ms grid. Re-evaluating the rule: for a duration D and period P, the number of ticks N = D/P. The action fires when the counter reaches N+1 because the first check is at t=0. Here D=30000ms, P=1000ms, so N=30. The threshold should be 30+1=31. The candidate used 30, causing early firing at 29 ticks (29000ms).
diagnosis.change_summary: Changed the wrapper period from 1000 to 100 ms to match the standard sustained-condition repair pattern (100 ms grid). Updated the threshold from 30 to 101 (30 seconds / 100 ms = 300 ticks + 1). This ensures the condition is held for exactly 30 seconds (300 ticks) before the action fires at t=30000 ms.
